newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bund futures seen adrift on EMU worries.
newsitem.headline: Bund futures seen adrift on EMU worries.

text.p: Bund futures were expected to spend Wednesday drifting sideways as the market awaited the next round of news on monetary union -- this time from Bonn.
The DTB September Bund future was up five basis points in early trade to 100.93 and was expected to move between 100.60 and 100.10 on the day.
"It is extremely slow moving," one trader said. "Apart from the long-end of the market, nothing much is happening.
The focus on EMU will shift to Bonn today where Dutch Prime Minister Wim Kok and Chancellor Helmut Kohl meet for talks ahead of the Amsterdam European Union sumit on June 16-17.
Finance Minister Theo Waigel will give a speech on tax and financial policy prior to the start of EMU at 1500 GMT.
Traders will be looking to see if Germany is willing to make a compromise on the stability pact which some fear France wants to water down to promote European jobs growth.

Otherwise there is little to focus on as Traders also have little to fear this afternoon from the U.S. where the indicator schedule looks thin until retail sales data are released at 1230 GMT on Thursday.
Traders may also chose to keep their powder dry ahead of the Bunesbank's regular council meeting on Thursday.
Some six out of 10 economists polled by Reuters on Tuesday said they expected the central bank to approve the government's asset revaluation plans at the meeting.
The yield curve, meanwhile, remains steady at around 232 basis points.
The cash benchmark 10-year Bund was eased slightly to 101.60 from 101.62 to yield 5.78 percent.
